module purpose: neorv32_sdi is a bus-controlled serial byte interface. It stores enable and interrupt settings from the bus, hands bus-written transmit bytes to an instantiated byte buffer, synchronizes the external serial pins, shifts a byte out on sdi_dat_o while sampling a byte in, and reports status or an interrupt request.

use-case flows.value: enable and interrupt-condition settings written into the control register
bus-written transmit byte delivered to the outgoing byte-buffer interface
serial-transfer start pulse that triggers a transmit-buffer read when chip select becomes active
serial shift-register load, bit shifting, input sampling, completion, and handoff of the completed byte to the incoming byte-buffer interface
interrupt request produced from enabled FIFO-status conditions
control/status fields or the received byte returned on a bus read, with a receive-buffer read strobe on data-register reads
control state, interrupt output, synchronizer state, and serial-engine state cleared by rstn_i; both byte-buffer interfaces cleared while ctrl.enable is low

conceptual assets.concept: SDI enable setting — whether the interface is active
conceptual assets.reasoning: The configure flow stores ctrl.enable from bus write data at line 133 under the bus-write qualification at lines 130-133. Integrity matters because this stored bit clears both byte-buffer interfaces when low (lines 200 and 239), gates interrupt reporting (line 249), and is copied into the serial-engine state (line 296). Availability is also established because the value is held until rewritten or reset and is returned on a control read at line 143. The bus request/response records carry a complete bus transaction and are not eligible structural references, so the internal register is the primary reference.

conceptual assets.concept: Interrupt-condition enable settings — which FIFO conditions may raise irq_o
conceptual assets.reasoning: The configure flow stores five interrupt-enable bits in ctrl.irq_rx_avail, ctrl.irq_rx_half, ctrl.irq_rx_full, ctrl.irq_tx_empty, and ctrl.irq_tx_nhalf at lines 135-139. The report flow uses those stored settings in the irq_o equation at lines 249-254, and control readback returns them at lines 147-151. Integrity matters because corrupt settings change which receive/transmit status conditions can assert irq_o; availability is also established because the settings persist until rewritten or reset.

conceptual assets.concept: Serial transfer progress state — the engine phase and bit position of an ongoing byte transfer
conceptual assets.reasoning: The serial-engine operate flow writes serial.state(2) from ctrl.enable at line 296, branches on case serial.state at line 297, clears serial.cnt in the load state at line 301, increments serial.cnt on sampled serial-clock activity at line 318, and uses serial.cnt(3) to choose completion or another shift phase at lines 328-332. Integrity matters because the implemented load, sample, shift, and completion order depends on these stored state values. Availability is also established under the RTL-visible conditions for progress: chip select active and sampled serial-clock transitions (lines 307, 317, and 326), with reset clearing state at lines 286-287.

conceptual assets.concept: Serial transfer start event — the pulse that begins a byte transfer by requesting transmit data
conceptual assets.reasoning: The start flow computes serial.start in state 100 when chip select is active: lines 307-309 set serial.start to '1' and move the engine into the next phase, while line 205 forwards that pulse to tx_fifo.re. Integrity matters because a wrong start pulse requests transmit data outside the implemented idle-and-chip-select-active condition. Availability is also established because the pulse is generated on the next clk_i edge when those conditions hold, and line 292 clears it otherwise.

conceptual assets.concept: Serial shift-register contents — the working byte that is loaded for output, shifted on each serial-clock event, and forwarded as received data at completion
conceptual assets.reasoning: The operate flow loads serial.sreg with zeros or tx_fifo.rdata in state 100 at lines 302-305, samples incoming serial data through sdi_dat_i into sync.sdi_ff at line 270 and serial.sdi_ff at line 314, then shifts serial.sreg left and appends the sampled bit at line 327. The MSB leaves the entity on sdi_dat_o at line 345, and the full byte is forwarded to rx_fifo.wdata at line 235. Integrity matters because both the outgoing serial bit stream and the completed received byte follow these load/shift rules. Availability is also established because reset initializes the register at line 288 and each active transfer updates it until completion. The transmit-source byte enters from tx_fifo.rdata, which is a carrier-only sub-unit output and is therefore not reported as a primary reference here.

conceptual assets.concept: Serial byte-complete event — indication that a full shifted byte is ready to be committed
conceptual assets.reasoning: The operate flow asserts serial.done only in state 111 when a sampled serial-clock event occurs and serial.cnt(3) = '1' at lines 327-330; line 236 forwards that pulse to rx_fifo.we. Integrity matters because this event decides when a full shifted byte may be committed to the incoming byte-buffer interface. Availability is also established because the pulse is generated exactly under the implemented terminal-count condition and is cleared at line 293 otherwise.

conceptual assets.concept: Interrupt request decision — whether the block reports an interrupt this cycle
conceptual assets.reasoning: The report flow registers irq_o from ctrl.enable and the enabled FIFO-status conditions at lines 249-254, with reset clearing it at line 247. Integrity matters because this is the module's external interrupt decision: corruption would falsely assert or suppress the reported interrupt condition. Availability is also established because with ctrl.enable = '1' and any selected condition true, the decision is delivered on the next rising edge of clk_i.
